name: Jamal Nasir
headline: Enthusiastic to build and create!
intro: I bring together economics, mathematics and code to solve real problems. I take a messy question, work out what actually needs answering, do the maths, and build something people can test and use. So far that has meant credit risk, electricity pricing, international trade, farming and language models. I learn new fields quickly and I see work through to the end.
highlights: PKR 5.5bn in guarantee facilities provided (about US$20 million)
€1 million Mitigation Action Facility grant, as relationship manager

points: Building forecasting and expected credit loss (ECL) models, which estimate how much a lender may lose on its loans, for assurance and valuation work. Reporting to the Partner.
Evaluated transactions and helped put in place guarantees of PKR 1.5bn with HBL Microfinance Bank and PKR 4.0bn with Bank Alfalah.
Relationship manager for a €1 million Mitigation Action Facility (MAF) grant: a returnable guarantee facility with LUMS for a swappable-battery programme.

Researched and modelled guarantees on electricity prices using data from the national grid operator (ISMO): how fixed prices, buyer contributions and reserves change what the guarantor could lose. This became “The price of a promise”.
Built and deployed an export analysis app that replaced repeated manual work.
Led Phase 2 of the Guarantee Management Portal, standardising the data and reports that partner banks submit.
Assessed the creditworthiness of 24 companies, mostly in energy and construction, looking at their debt, cash, ability to pay interest and cash flows.

experience.organization: Project Indigenous Mechanization · Government of Punjab
points: Worked with Dr. Shakeel Sadiq Jajja on locally made electric farm machinery. Spoke with 50+ farmers, manufacturers and lenders to understand what holds adoption back and where the opportunities are.
Co-developed IBA’s five-year strategic plan across seven pillars, designed targets that match accreditation requirements, and supported data modelling and performance dashboards.
Delivered forecasting and classification systems for clients in Ireland.
Built differential-equation models to forecast how many cattle Irish farmland can support; mentored the team on an image-recognition project.
Earned more than €7,000 in consulting fees.

projects.title: The price of a promise
projects.description: What does it cost to promise a buyer a fixed electricity price for a year? A simulation built on real grid demand and cost data that shows how much the guarantor could lose, and how large a reserve it needs.
projects.methods: Historical replay · Scenario simulation · Reserve sizing

projects.title: Pakistan export intelligence
projects.description: A live app that replaces repeated manual analysis. It shows what Pakistan exports, how concentrated its exporters are, and where new markets could be.

projects.title: Credit and guarantee reviews
projects.description: Reviewed 24 energy and construction companies and guarantee deals worth PKR 5.5bn: reading the accounts, testing the assumptions, and giving a clear view of the risk.
projects.methods: Financial analysis · Cash-flow review · Risk assessment

projects.title: Loan servicing risk alerts
projects.description: Early-warning models that flag microfinance borrowers likely to fall behind, so loan officers can step in sooner. I found the warning signs in the data and helped design how the model would be used day to day.

projects.title: TinyLlama: fine-tuning and alignment
projects.description: Fine-tuned a small open-source language model (1.1 billion parameters) for more natural conversation using everyday dialogue data, and tested how well it follows instructions and answers questions.

projects.title: Option pricing and simulation
projects.description: Priced options with the Black–Scholes and Heston models, and checked the results against Monte Carlo simulations on Indian stock market (NSE) data.

projects.title: Optimisation in high dimensions
projects.description: Worked through the maths behind common optimisation methods, then built and compared several models for prediction problems with many variables.

Excel, Power BI, Microsoft Azure, Git, LaTeX, EViews, MATLAB, Stata, SPSS

Modelling, simulation and data work in finance, energy, development and machine learning.
Credit assessment, guarantee design, and expected credit loss and valuation models.
